hypothesis: The reservation step guards createReservationItems with Modules.LOCKING. I expect two distinct carts on different servers, each wanting one OVS-SOLO (stock 1), to both complete with orders, producing a live reservation sum of 2 against stock 1 and an oversell.

Control case: the same SOLO race on one server. Within a single process the in-memory lock should serialize the two reservation calls, so I expect only one order and no oversell. A pass here, together with the two-server attempt, would point at the cross-process lock rather than general reservation logic.

A cart with OVS-PIECE qty 1 and OVS-TWOPACK qty 1 both use the shared WIDGET item (stock 10). Two such carts, each needing 3 units, total 6 units, which fits in 10. To expose a per-line miss I instead use stock WIDGET 4: each cart needs 3 units, so only one can fit. If each line is checked against stock alone and entries sharing WIDGET are not summed, both carts could complete, giving live reservations of 6 against stock 4 and an oversell.

Ten carts, each wanting one OVS-SOLO (stock 1), are split across two servers and completed together. Under a process-local in-memory lock, the two servers can each see the SOLO unit as free and both create reservations, so more than one order is accepted and the live reservation sum exceeds stock 1. The count of carts raises the chance that the two processes interleave.
